# Derived figures (generated by ratios.mjs)

## Hash cost per 32 bytes of digest vs what 32 proof bytes buy (25,600 op-cost, 16 standard hash iterations)

| hash (2-to-1 node) | digest B | op-cost per node (std) | per 32 B of digest | x 25,600 | hash iterations per 32 B (of 16) | extra proof bytes |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SHA-256, native: OP_CAT OP_SHA256 (K17) | 32 | 680 | 680 | 0.03 | 2.0 | – |
| SHA-256 Merkle level, branchless, h=32 (K6) | 32 | 812 | 812 | 0.03 | 2.0 | – |
| SHA-256 path level incl. index bit, h=32 (K6, 20-level run / 20) | 32 | 1,938 | 1,938 | 0.08 | 2.0 | – |
| SHA-256 path level incl. index bit, h=25 (K6, 20-level run / 20) | 25 | 2,059 | 2,635 | 0.10 | 1.3 | – |
| Blake2s compression, unrolled (Stwo) | 32 | 837,797 | 837,797 | 32.73 | 0.0 | – |
| Blake2s compression, G as function (Stwo) | 32 | 961,245 | 961,245 | 37.55 | 0.0 | – |
| RPO permutation, inverse S-box computed (Miden) | 32 | 4,966,796 | 4,966,796 | 194.02 | 0.0 | – |
| RPO permutation, inverse S-box witnessed (Miden) | 32 | 1,053,526 | 1,053,526 | 41.15 | 0.0 | 672 (buys 537,600) |
| Tip5 permutation (Triton) | 40 | 756,986 | 605,589 | 23.66 | 0.0 | – |

Consensus mode charges 64 instead of 192 per iteration; the emulated hashes use no hash iterations, so their figures are the same in both modes.

## GF(2^128) multiplication against prime-field multiplication (standard op-cost)

| GF(2^128) variant | op-cost | / Goldilocks mulmod | / 128-bit prime mulmod | / Goldilocks^2 mul | / Goldilocks^3 mul |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| bit-serial | 460,668 | 809.3 | 373.3 | 126.0 | 57.1 |
| 4-bit windowed (table built per mul) | 117,009 | 205.6 | 94.8 | 32.0 | 14.5 |
| 4-bit windowed, table reused (minus build) | 100,031 | 175.7 | 81.1 | 27.4 | 12.4 |

Reference prime-field costs: Goldilocks mulmod 569, 128-bit prime mulmod 1,234, Goldilocks^2 mul 3,657, Goldilocks^3 mul 8,064.

## Per-query composition for the P128 shape (k0 = 4, folds 4, 8, 8, final degree < 2^8, h = 32, b = 8): sum of measured kernels

| step | kernel op-cost | count | subtotal |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| query index from G (K5) | 1,427 | 1 | 1,427 |
| x0 = 7 w^v and x0^-1 (K4, 4-bit windows, twice) | 13,224 | 2 | 26,448 |
| leaf hash + parse: trace 64 B (K7) | 6,913 | 1 | 6,913 |
| leaf hash + parse: comp, fri1, fri2 192 B (K7) | 21,178 | 3 | 63,533 |
| Merkle levels kept in the query blob: 4 trees x b = 8 (K6 per level) | 1,938 | 32 | 62,010 |
| DEEP denominators 1/(x - z), 1/(x - wz), 4 points (K3, witnessed norm inverse) | 13,366 | 8 | 106,925 |
| DEEP value f0 at 4 points (K10) | 42,359 | 4 | 169,438 |
| fold arity 4 (K11, IDFT) | 57,213 | 1 | 57,213 |
| fold arity 8, twice (K11, binary folds) | 134,686 | 2 | 269,371 |
| final polynomial, 256 coefficients (K12, best variant, net of cleanup) | 706,281 | 1 | 706,281 |
| **total per query (excluding fold consistency compares, loop glue and the multiproof above the cap)** | | | **1,469,558** |

The design model (params.py OPC) puts a P128 query at 994,928 (b = 8). With a final degree < 2^5 instead of 2^8 the final-polynomial line drops to 87,162 (measured, 32 coefficients) and the total to 850,439.

Per-input fixed costs (measured): transcript P100 129,412; transcript P128 164,175; AIR identity at z 334,043; code load 4,000 B (libauth; BCHN +4,000) 25,270; read 1,000 B from a 10 KB sibling 27,805; final polynomial from a 6,144-byte blob into 768 numbers (net of cleanup) 610,544; final polynomial as 768 pushed numbers bound by hashing the own unlocking (net of cleanup) 37,546.

## Multiproof merge (K8) and a projection for P128 in one input (layout b)

- Merge cost per processed node, h = 32, standard: blob bookkeeping 15,592; entries as stack items 5,103 (43 positions, 16 levels). A plain path level costs 1,938.
- Expected nodes processed by full multiproofs for P128 (43 uniform queries, trees of depth 19, 19, 16, 13): 2,134.
- Projection: 43 x 1,407,548 (query work without in-blob levels) + 2,134 x 5,103 (merge) + 535,764 (transcript, AIR at z, final-polynomial binding) = **71,948,960** standard op-cost, against 76,532,000 (TXv5-as-written, base 41) and 84,499,200 (bch-spec) for the 95,624-byte unlocking: 94.0% and 85.1%. Loop glue and fold consistency compares are not included.

## Layout (a): queries per standard input (P128 shape, kernel sums)

- 94% of a full input's budget: 7,550,831. Measured per-input fixed work for a query input: transcript 164,175 + code load 4,000 B 29,270 (BCHN-adjusted) + reading the 6.4 KB PT 30,803 + parsing its 768 final-polynomial values 610,544 = 834,792.
- With 1,469,558 per query (b = 8): 4 queries per input (6,668 B of query blobs), so op-cost, not bytes, limits a query input. With a final degree < 2^5: 8 queries by op-cost (parse of 96 values estimated at 70,000, not measured), more than the 5 query blobs of 1,667 B that fit in 10,000 B: bytes bind again.
